scenario.title: Lakeside Water — billing dispute surge (Mock #6, not an official contest problem)
scenario.description: Billing dispute tickets roughly doubled in August-September. Customer Service wants an AI agent. Field reading is contracted out; AMI meters and the meter data management system (MDMS) are run by a vendor.
scenario.initial_request: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

potential_bias: frames the issue as a response-speed problem

P-M2C.name: meter-to-cash
steps: read collection (AMI interval read or field manual read)
estimate substitution when no accepted read

DA-RULES.name: billing import validation rule change log

F-02.statement: Route completion for Aug‑Sep is 0.88 with a target of 0.95 and 9,200 manual read accounts.

F-03.statement: Tariff change log contains zero records.

F-04.statement: Disputed bills by read type: ESTIMATED 1240, ACTUAL 1785.

F-05.statement: Dispute response times: median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days, SLA 3.0 days, tickets 2,440.

CL-01.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August. Build an AI agent that auto-answers billing dispute tickets and fixes whatever is causing the wrong bills.

CL-02.statement: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

CL-03.statement: There has been no tariff change this year.

H-REQ-FRAME-AI-AGENT.statement: Dispute tickets doubled since August; the appropriate response is an AI agent that auto-answers tickets and corrects underlying billing errors.

H-AMI-READ-FAILURE.statement: Increased AMI read errors or missing reads since August lead to estimation substitutions and incorrect bills, driving dispute tickets.

H-FIELD-READ-ISSUE.statement: Field manual read processes deteriorated (missed reads, unconfirmed route changes) after August, causing estimation errors and billing disputes.

H-BILLING-RULE-CHANGE.statement: Changes to billing import validation rules since August introduced systematic mis‑billing, generating the dispute surge.

interpretation_history.interpretation: Observation shows dispute ticket volume rose from ~610 in June and 590 in July to 1,180 in August and 1,260 in September, confirming a roughly two‑fold increase starting in August. This validates the claim that dispute tickets doubled since August but does not indicate the underlying cause.
Route completion for August‑September is 0.88, below the 0.95 target, indicating sub‑optimal field manual read performance.
The tariff change log shows no recorded tariff changes, indicating that tariff modifications are not a source of the billing dispute surge.

The observation shows that disputed bills are roughly split between estimated (1240) and actual (1785) reads, indicating that the dispute surge is not limited to estimation errors; actual‑read bills also generate many disputes.

E-05.content: We are short three readers since July; routes run late, so those customers get estimated bills.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports a shortage of three field readers since July, causing routes to run late and resulting in estimated bills for affected customers. This suggests field staffing issues may be contributing to estimation errors and subsequent disputes.

The dispute response times remain within the SLA (median 1.6 days, p90 2.8 days < SLA 3.0 days) despite a high volume of 2,440 tickets, indicating that the surge in disputes is not causing delayed responses.

E-07.content: There has been no tariff change this year.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The stakeholder reports no tariff change this year, indicating that tariff modifications are not a source of the billing dispute surge.

E-08.content: Service contract §4.2: utility may request route priority changes; executed after Field Operations Manager confirmation.

interpretation_history.interpretation: The observation confirms that route priority changes require Field Operations Manager confirmation, aligning with the existing dispatch approval constraint.

U-SPECIFIC-RULE-CHANGE.question: Which specific rule(s) in the billing import validation rule change log caused the mis‑billing?
U-SPECIFIC-RULE-CHANGE.resolution_path: Audit the billing-config change log to pinpoint altered rules and test their impact on bill calculations using a sandbox.
U-SPECIFIC-RULE-CHANGE.safe_placeholder: Continue operating under the current rule set while monitoring dispute volume; any rule change will be deployed via a controlled config change after validation.

U-EFFECTIVENESS-OF-FIX.question: Will correcting the identified rule(s) reduce dispute volume to pre‑August baseline across all customer segments?
U-EFFECTIVENESS-OF-FIX.resolution_path: After deploying the corrected rule set, track weekly dispute ticket counts and compare to the June‑July baseline.
U-EFFECTIVENESS-OF-FIX.safe_placeholder: Track dispute ticket volume weekly; if volume does not decline after rule correction, investigate additional causes.

A-NO-TARIFF-CHANGE.statement: No tariff changes occurred during the period, so tariff is not a contributing factor.

A-FIELD-READ-NOT-CAUSE.statement: Field manual read performance did not deteriorate enough to explain the dispute surge.

G-1.statement: dispute volume back to pre-August baseline with correct bills
